items.lawCode: Amd §453, Gen Bus L; amd §§209 & 141, Soc Serv L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3377

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the general business law and the social services law,
in relation to irrevocable trust accounts for funeral and burial
expenses


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill closes an unintended loophole in the pre-need funeral and
Medicaid statutes to ensure that any pre-need funeral account that is
established by an applicant or recipient of Medicaid/SSI to pre-pay
the funeral/burial expenses of a family member must be irrevocable.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Amends Subparagraph (d) of Subdivision 1, Subparagraph (f) of
Subdivision 3 and Subparagraph (g) of Subdivision 3 of Section 453 of
the General Business law, as well as Subdivision 6 of Section 141 and
Subsection 6 of Section 209 of the Social Services Law. The bill
would:

* Ensure that all funds placed in pre-need accounts that are opened by
a Medicaid/551 applicant or recipient for the eventual use by their
family members would actually be used for this purpose.

* Provide that this requirement is incorporated in the current legal
disclosures that must be included in all irrevocable pre-need funeral
agreements.

*Similarly provide that this new family member provision is
incorporated in the current requirement that relates to the language
contained in promotional literature dealing with irrevocable
funeral/burial accounts.

*Ensure consistency with current law by clarifying that any funds
remaining in an irrevocable account after the payment of all
funeral/burial expenses will be transmitted to the social services
official of the county or, as appropriate, other local government
subdivision where the person opening the account resided at the time
of their death.

*Apply to all funeral/burial accounts established on or after January
1, 2010, the effective date of the bill.

 JUSTIFICATION :
New York State law has long afforded individuals the option to pay
their funeral/burial costs in advance by formally establishing what
are known as "pre-need accounts". These accounts are strictly
regulated and appropriately provide the consumer with various rights
and disclosures in relation to the funds he or she has deposited for
this sole purpose. Indeed, consumers are choosing to do so more often
for their own peace of mind as well as to spare their loved ones an
additional burden at an emotionally wrenching time.

Current law requires that these accounts must be established as
"revocable trusts", but requires that they be "irrevocable trusts" in
nature if opened by an individual who is an applicant for or recipient
of Medicaid or SSI to pay their own funeral/burial expenses.

Recently, however, a growing trend has become apparent where
Medicaid/SSI applicants or clients are establishing pre-need funeral
accounts for the benefit of their family members as part of the
"spend-down" process so they become eligible for Medicaid/SSI.
(Because the family member beneficiary was not a Medicaid/SSI
applicant or recipient, the account, by law must be revocable.)

However, it has been discovered that, in these particular cases,
almost all of these pre-need accounts were immediately closed once the
person who had opened them (the "purchaser") died. This reflects the
fact that this practice is increasingly being encouraged as simply a
tool for a person to spend-down their assets for Medicaid eligibility,
but without any intent whatsoever to actually use these pre-need funds
to pay the funeral and burial expenses of the purchaser's family
member(s). In essence, funeral directors' time is increasingly being
used to make funeral pre-arrangements and establish pre-need accounts
that were ostensibly opened to help family members, but, in reality,
are never going to be used for that purpose.

This bill is simply intended to deter this practice by making
irrevocable all pre-need funeral accounts established and funded by an
applicant/recipient of Medicaid or SSI for a family member (as defined
in Federal Medicaid program guidelines). In this way, the funds' use
would be restricted to its proper purpose. It is hoped that then only
those individuals with the true intention of establishing pre-need
accounts to pay funeral and burial expenses would actually do so.

Notably, this bill would not in any way impact the rights of a funeral
consumer or the legal protections afforded his or her pre-need funds.
New York State is second-to-none when it comes to protecting our
consumers in this area, and should take great pride in this
achievement and standing.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Should result in some Medicaid cost savings for the State and
counties, which will also receive the balance of any funds remaining
in an "irrevocable family member account".

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect January 1, 2010 and apply to these types of
accounts established on or after this date.
